title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། མེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 185)
shelf_note: Pramāṇa commentary folio (refutation of establishing a prior cognition via memory and arthāpatti; svasaṃvedana argument), consistent with the Derge Tshad ma section.

ocr_errors.image: སྐྱེས་བུ་གཞན་གྱིས་མྱོང་བར་གྱུར་པའི་དོན་ (line 5, as far as the print reads)
ocr_errors.problem: genitive read as ནི; sense recoverable, both translations construe it correctly
particle form uncertain at this resolution; no change of sense

tr_errors_A.english: that experience by another does not belong to another person because there is no experience; just as an external person has not experienced the object
tr_errors_A.problem: closing analogy garbled: 'does not belong to another person' inverts whose experience is lacking, and ཕ་རོལ་པོ ('the other person') rendered 'external person'; the point (the other's experience is not one's own) is obscured

tr_errors_A.english: To this, the commentary states: "That too..."
tr_errors_A.problem: the lemma is from the root text, not 'the commentary'

tr_errors_A.english: because the external object is hidden
there is no experience of presumption distinct from memory

tr_errors_B.english: just as that other person does not experience the object for you
tr_errors_B.problem: 'for you' is an interpretive addition, though it states the intended point

tr_errors_B.english: because memory occurs as a mere mental event
an experience must be self-aware to be valid
tr_errors_B.problem: summary slightly mis-states the thesis (self-experience is needed for memory to be possible)

pages.prefer_reason: Neither version has a serious error; B renders the closing analogy of another person's experience coherently where A garbles it (moderate), and A's Sanskrit glossing is not a fidelity advantage.

adjudication.claim: closing example garbled ('does not belong to another person', 'external person')
adjudication.why: Image line 8 reads གཞན་དེས་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བ་ནི། སྐྱེས་བུ་གཞན་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་སྐྱེས་བུ་ཕ་རོལ་པོས་དོན་ཉམས་སུ་མ་མྱོང་བ; A's rendering misattributes the lack of experience and mistranslates ཕ་རོལ་པོ; moderate, not a reversal of the page's thesis.

adjudication.claim: OCR ཐ་མ་ should be ཐལ་བ་, making 'final consequence/conclusion' a derived error in both
adjudication.why: At this resolution line 5 reads ཐམ/ཐ་མ as transcribed; cannot confirm ཐལ་བ, and in any case it affects A and B equally and is minor.

adjudication.claim: A preferable for precise Sanskrit terminology and structural cues
adjudication.why: Glossing quality is not fidelity; on the Tibetan, A's final passage is the only moderate error on the page and B has none.

adjudication.claim: 'for you' added in the closing analogy
adjudication.why: Not in the Tibetan, but an interpretive addition consistent with the argument; minor.

book_verdict: Clean Derge woodblock folio with a near-exact transcription; both translations follow the argument without serious error, B being clearer in the closing analogy.
